fatal_errors: The intervention is not concretely specified: no secondary-phase chemistry, concentration, processing route, or microstructural target is given, so it cannot be reproducibly tested.
The hidden intervention was variation of Mo content within an existing Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composite, not addition of an unspecified self-lubricating phase to monolithic CoCrFeNi.
The baseline is incorrect: the relevant comparison was the Mo0.2 composite rather than unreinforced monolithic CoCrFeNi.
The prediction of lower friction and wear at every temperature misses the observed composition-dependent tradeoff and severe intermediate-temperature wear peak.
The proposed falsification rule based on a majority of conditions does not test the stronger claim of maintaining improvement throughout the full temperature range.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad wide-temperature tribology problem and invokes adaptive tribofilm formation, which partially resembles the high-temperature oxide/silver-molybdate glaze mechanism. However, it does not reconstruct the actual Mo-content intervention, Mo-induced lattice distortion and sigma-phase strengthening, or the distinct low-temperature MoS2/Ag and high-temperature oxide/molybdate lubrication regimes. Test conditions are left generic instead of specifying air, an 8 N load, Si3N4 counterface, sliding speed, and distance. It also omits the important 200–400 °C thermal-softening and wear maximum, uses the wrong baseline, and supplies no concrete prior evidence. Because the secondary phase is undefined, even the otherwise reasonable comparative experiment is not reproducible or strongly discriminating.
